judge_assessment.explanation: Both hard failures and the page-flow error check out. Problem 7 prints 'Explain in words what Mia did wrong' and verify.json id 7 is a lone eval (13-5 -> 8); problem 2 prints 'Draw the counters she still needs' and id 2 is a lone solve; problem 4 prints 'First write the subtraction sentence that finds the missing part. Then solve it.' and id 4 records only the value 9 -- while final_response.md states '16 verified, 0 manual'. Confirmed. Page flow: pdfinfo gives worksheet.pdf 4 pages and page 4 carries only problem 8, exactly as described. I would add one item the judge missed -- problem 6 also says 'Write the equation you used', a third uncovered printed slot. The mathematics is right throughout: 4, 5, 6, 9, 7, 8, 8, then 8 and 5 with 8 > 5, plus study-guide try-its 7, 9, 7. REJECT is correct on either ground.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 8 is the model for what the rest of the sheet should have done: it prints three responses and verify.json declares three entries under id 8 (solve x+6-14 -> 8, solve 9+x-14 -> 5, compare 14-6 vs 14-9 -> '>'). Keep that structure -- it is the working example of the fix the other problems need.

The pedagogical payoff the key draws from problem 8 is worth preserving verbatim: 'both equations have the same whole, so the bigger known part leaves the smaller missing part.' That turns a comparison exercise into a structural observation about part-part-whole.

Every key solution shows BOTH routes -- count on from the known part and subtract from the whole -- and then checks by adding back. For missing addends specifically, that dual presentation is the whole point, because the count-on route is what a first-grader has and the subtraction route is where they are going.

Problem 6 declares answer_unit 'cubes' and the answer line prints 'Answer: ____ cubes', bound by the unit gate -- units are stated on the one problem that has them, and not faked on the ones that do not.

root_causes.description: SKILL.md actively steers error-analysis items away from 'manual': 'error-analysis ("find and fix the mistake") via the ordinary types --- the planted wrong result is checkably wrong and the correction checkably right. Reserve `manual` for genuinely open reasoning.' A find-and-fix item has TWO halves: the correction (checkable) and the diagnosis (not). The instruction covers only the first half, so the generator types the whole problem as eval/solve and the honest manual flag is never raised.
evidence: worksheet problem 7: 'Explain in words what Mia did wrong.' -- verify.json id 7 is a lone eval (13-5 -> 8)
worksheet problem 2: 'Draw the counters she still needs, then finish the sentence.' -- verify.json id 2 is a lone solve (8+x-13 -> 5)

root_causes.description: The coverage contract is stated per PROBLEM, not per printed RESPONSE SLOT. SKILL.md's JSON-format section says verification 'hard-fails unless every problem id 1..N has at least one check', and verify.py enforces exactly that. One check therefore discharges a problem that prints two or three separate things for the student to write, and the gate chain reports the sheet as fully verified.
evidence: worksheet problem 4: 'First write the subtraction sentence that finds the missing part. Then solve it.' -- verify.json id 4 is one eval (16-7 -> 9); the sentence '16 - 7 = ___' the key states is never bound
worksheet problem 6: 'How many blue cubes does he still need? Write the equation you used.' -- verify.json id 6 is one eval (20-12 -> 8); the equation slot is uncovered
the same file shows the pattern works: id 8 carries three entries (solve -> 8, solve -> 5, compare -> '>'), one per printed response

root_causes.description: Two independent bank defects collide in a single line here: entry 8 reads '8, 5, ---'. The intermediate solves are concatenated with the answer, and the verified '>' renders as the em-dash that the module reserves for manual items.
evidence: verify.json id 8's third entry: compare, order 'relation', expected '>'

root_causes.description: Eight short K-1 items are spread over four pages with problem 8 alone on page 4. Nothing in the gate chain penalises a sparse trailing page; scripts/page_budget.py only enforces an upper cap.
evidence: page 4 of worksheet.pdf contains problem 8 and nothing else

improvements.title: Explanations and drawn/marked work must be declared manual, not folded into a numeric check
improvements.proposed_change: Amend SKILL.md so that a find-and-fix or error-analysis item is declared as TWO entries under one id: the ordinary typed check for the correction, plus a `manual` entry whose `desc` states the full-credit diagnosis. Extend the same rule to any stem containing 'explain', 'tell what ... did wrong', 'draw', 'cross out', 'circle', 'show your work' or 'write the equation'. Back it with a lint in tests/check_layout.py that scans problem prose for those verbs and fails when the matching id carries no `manual` entry. Here: id 7 needs a manual entry for the explanation of Mia's error, and id 2 needs one for the drawn counters.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture: a worksheet whose problem 2 reads 'Explain what she did wrong, then write the correct answer' with a verify JSON holding only an eval entry for id 2. Assert the build exits non-zero (or exit 2 with problem 2 listed as manual). Today the chain exits 0 and the delivery text claims '0 manual'.
improvements.expected_impact: Problem 7 becomes an honestly flagged manual item and the '0 manual' claim disappears, which is the primary hard failure on this case.
improvements.risk: Medium: a verb lint over prose will produce false positives (a stem that says 'draw' inside a worked hint). Ship it as exit-2 manual visibility rather than exit-1, which is the honest outcome anyway and cannot block a correct build.

improvements.title: Every printed response slot needs its own verification entry, not one per problem
improvements.proposed_change: Change the coverage rule from 'one check per problem id' to 'one check per printed response slot'. Concretely: (a) rewrite the SKILL.md JSON-format sentence to require an entry for every blank, box or \ansblank the item prints, using a `manual` entry when a slot is a mark or a sentence; (b) have tests/check_layout.py count the response macros inside each \problem segment and fail when that count exceeds the number of verify entries carrying that id. The schema already supports several entries per id -- Problems 4 and 6 each print an equation slot beyond the value; id 8 in this same file already shows the three-entries-under-one-id pattern.
improvements.regression_test: Add a fixture worksheet whose problem 1 prints two \ansblank slots with a verify JSON carrying a single entry for id 1, and assert check_layout.py exits non-zero naming problem 1. It passes (exit 0) today, which is the defect.
improvements.expected_impact: The subtraction sentence in problem 4 and the equation in problem 6 get bound, so the key's stated '16 - 7 = ___' is verified rather than merely asserted.
improvements.risk: Medium. Counting response macros will initially fire on sheets that print a decorative underline, and on the 'Answer:' line that some templates emit in addition to an inline blank. Land the checker in warn-only mode for one run, tune against the existing eval corpus, then make it a hard gate.

improvements.title: Quick Answers bank prints an em-dash instead of the verified > / < relation
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_quick_answers.py, _fmt() sends every string 'expected' through sympy.sympify(); '>' and '<' raise SympifyError and fall through to the '---' branch, which the module's own docstring reserves for 'see solution' / manual-only ids. Add a relation branch before the sympify attempt: map the bare relation tokens ('>', '<', '>=', '<=', '=', '≥', '≤') to their math-mode LaTeX ($>$, $<$, $\ge$, $\le$, $=$) and return that. Everything else keeps its current behaviour, so genuinely manual ids still print '---' and remain distinguishable from a verified relation.
improvements.regression_test: Add a case to tests/test_render_quick_answers.py that renders a verify JSON containing {"id": 1, "type": "compare", "values": ["5+3", "4+2"], "order": "relation", "expected": ">"} alongside a {"id": 2, "type": "manual"} entry, and asserts the bank line for id 1 contains '$>$' while the line for id 2 is '---'. It fails today because both render '---'.
improvements.expected_impact: Every worksheet whose verification_targets include 'compare' with order 'relation' regains real entries in the grader's at-a-glance bank. In this shard alone that is curr-002 (2 of 10 entries), curr-006 (2 of 8), curr-032 (2 of 10), curr-038 (part of entry 8) and curr-050 (2 of 10).
improvements.risk: Low and contained to the bank. The entries are plain text by design and are never read by check_answer_key.py, so the strict per-problem binding gate cannot be affected. Only risk is choosing a LaTeX spelling that does not compile, which the existing compile-ak gate would catch immediately.

improvements.title: Reject a worksheet whose last page carries a single short problem
improvements.proposed_change: scripts/page_budget.py currently only enforces an upper page cap. Add a density check: fail (or exit 2) when the final page holds one problem and less than roughly a third of its text block is used. The fix at authoring time is to trim per-problem workspace_cm by 0.5-1 cm across the sheet so the tail problem pulls up onto the previous page.
improvements.regression_test: Add a fixture PDF/log in tests/test_page_budget.py whose last page has one problem and >65% whitespace, and assert page_budget.py reports it. It is silent today.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes the mostly-blank trailing page that cost visual_and_print_quality points on curr-038 (page 4 holds only problem 8) and curr-050 (page 5 holds only problem 10), and shortens K-1 sheets generally.
improvements.risk: Low, but the threshold must not force a problem's workspace below the minimum the layout gate already enforces; make the two checks agree before enabling.

case_summary: The missing-addend sequence itself is well built -- ten-frame, two ten-frames, number bond, subtraction rewrite, tape-diagram cube train, a unit-tagged story, an error analysis, and a two-equation challenge -- and every value recomputes correctly. Two independent grounds for rejection. First, the trust boundary: the drawn counters (problem 2), the written subtraction sentence (problem 4), the written equation (problem 6, which the judge did not name) and the explanation of Mia's error (problem 7) are all outside the verification record while the delivery text claims '16 verified, 0 manual'. Second, page flow: eight short items over four pages with problem 8 alone on the last one. Two smaller things: Quick Answers entry 8 prints '8, 5, ---', showing both bank defects at once, and the key's problem 6 contains a garbled sentence ('Take 12 from 20: 20 make ten first, 20 - 10 = 10, then 10 - 2 = 8') that should be reworded.
